source_refs.note: Topic 8.5, printed page 171 (Figure 8.2, carried by the dynamic equilibrium original), with Quick Check 8.3 (c) as the self-check.

items: The state of equilibrium applies only to reversible reactions.
Equilibrium can be established only if the reaction vessel is closed, so that no part of the reactants or products escapes.

blocks.text: For CaCO3(s) giving CaO(s) + CO2(g), equilibrium is established in a closed system but cannot be established in an open system.

blocks.alt: Two vessels containing red balls of CaCO3(s), green balls of CaO(s) and small grey balls of CO2(g). (a) A closed vessel: a mixture of CaCO3 and CaO at the bottom with CO2 trapped above. (b) A vessel open at the top: almost all the solid is CaO and CO2 escapes from the mouth. Under each vessel: CaCO3(s) ⇌ CaO(s) + CO2(g). A key below.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.2: (a) Equilibrium is established when the system is closed (b) Equilibrium can not be established in the open system (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 8.2).
